newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian parties sign fair election deal.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parties sign fair election deal.

text.p: Albania's three main political parties signed an agreement on Monday pledging to ensure a free and fair general election on Sunday and to work for stable and democratic government, a Roman Catholic peace group said.

The "Pact for the Future of Albania", signed at the Sant'Egidio Community in Rome, also recognised the need for a coalition government after Sunday's vote and said the opposition would be entitled to hold key watchdog positions in parliament.

The four-point agreement was signed by the chairman of President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party, Tritan Shehu, the leader of the main opposition Socialist Party, Fatos Nano, and Skender Gjinushi of the Social Democratic Party.

The leaders of two smaller parties, Sabri Godo of the Republican Party and Hysen Selfo of the rightist National Front, attended the ceremony. Sant'Egidio officials said they did not sign the document out of respect for many other tiny parties which were not represented.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in Albania, Europe's poorest country, since the beginning of the year in unrest that began with popular anger over the collapse of shady savings schemes.
About 50 people have died in the past week alone as the campaign for Sunday's general election draws to a close.

Signatories to Monday's accord promised to conduct the remainder of the campaign "according to the standards of correct political dialogue, avoiding any violence that obstructs freedom of movement and of the expression of political ideas".
"The solution to the grave crisis which Albania is going through...depends on the free and fair conduct of the elections on June 29, 1997," the accord said.

"It is only on this condition that the electoral results, confirmed by the international community, will be incontestable and respected not only by our political parties but, above all, by the Albanian people throughout the country," it said.
The Democratic Party is defending a huge parliamentary majority won in a general election last year which both Albania's opposition and Western observers denounced as unfair.
Berisha was pressured in March to agree to Sunday's early election and to the appointment of a multi-party government led by the Socialists after a rebellion in the south of the country.
Rioters looted weapons from depots and for several days Albania was on the brink of anarchy.
A 7,000-strong multinational peacekeeping force has also been deployed in the Balkan state but gangs still roam many roads and some areas elude control of authorities.
Scores of international observers will monitor voting.
Monday's accord recognised that "the grave situation in which the country finds itself requires the attention of all parties in the framework of commonly agreed political cooperation".

"We therefore recognise the priority of a real coalition government in which the majority party would be flanked by other parties deeply interested in the institutional and economic reconstruction of the country," the agreement read.

It said the opposition would have the right to hold institutional positions such as the chairmanship of many parliamentary commissions, a vice-presidency of parliament and the chairmanship of Albania's state control commission.
